subject: Rebalance request: shifting seats & feature-credit options for PulseHealth
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia@pulsehealth.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Victor Chen <vchen@pulsehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging question — credits & seat rebalancing

Hi Rishi,

Quick question as we prep our budget for H2: we signed for 500 seats on the Standard bundle but usage is spikier than expected. The team wants to move ~120 heavy-inference seats onto Pro for steady low-latency, and scale the rest down to a compact Standard that keeps embeddings only where possible.

Two asks:
- Can we reassign seats across tiers within the same contract period without full re-pricing?
- Can unused seat capacity be converted to feature credits (e.g., extra GBs of KV cache / accelerated inference credits) rather than refunded?

Victor also asked if there are recommended packaging patterns for mixed-hosting (some workloads private, some hosted) — we want to avoid double-charging or duplicate feature fees.

Attaching our MAA spreadsheet with current seat assignments.

Thanks,
Olivia

--
Olivia Park
Head of AI Ops, PulseHealth
olivia@pulsehealth.com
(415) 555-0192
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Victor Chen <vchen@pulsehealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging question — credits & seat rebalancing

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear note and the MAA. Short answers up front: yes on in-contract seat reassignment (with limited re-pricing rules), and yes we can convert unused committed seats into directional feature credits for a rolling 12-month window. A few details and options below.

What we can do today (options):
1) Seat-tier swap (no commit change):
   - Move up to 30% of committed seats across tiers each quarter without renegotiation. Beyond that we apply a pro-rated delta for the remainder.
   - This preserves your committed pricing band and avoids a full re-rate.

2) Seat-to-credit conversion:
   - Unused Standard seats can be converted to Feature Credits at a 0.7x monetary conversion (i.e., $1,000 of unused commitment -> $700 of credits). Credits can be redeemed for:
     * KV cache GB-hours premium
     * Accelerated inference tokens (Preferred GPU queue)
     * Extra eval/quality-run credits
   - Credits expire 12 months from issuance.

3) Mixed-hosting guidance (private vs hosted):
   - We don’t double-bill for the same feature if you dedicate capacity in Private and host dev/test on Redwood Hosted under the same account. You can route by workload tag and we’ll apply a single feature credit pool.
   - Exception: Dedicated Private capacity incurs an infra uplift; credits can offset feature/service fees but not the infra uplift.

Recommended path for PulseHealth (given your ask to move ~120 seats to Pro):
- Approve a 90-seat immediate swap within the quarterly 30% window (no re-rate).
- Convert the remaining 30 seats you won’t use this quarter into feature credits (convert at 0.7x).
- We’ll provide a 60-day trial of Accelerated Inference on 40 seats so you can validate latency impact before fully committing.

Next steps I suggest:
- I’ll send a short contract amendment with the swap and credit line item (PDF).
- Monica (CC’d) will outline the migration plan and the migration credits available for the private-hosted transition.

Attaching a draft proposal (PDF) that shows pricing math and example credit allocation. Happy to jump on a 30-min call this week to walk through.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
(650) 555-0128
From: Olivia Park <olivia@pulsehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Victor Chen <vchen@pulsehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging question — credits & seat rebalancing

Thanks Rishi — this reads well and the 60-day trial is exactly what we needed to validate. A couple of follow-ups:
- Can the 0.7x conversion be bumped to 0.8x if we commit to a 12-month renewal on the consolidated package?
- For the trial, can those 40 seats be part of our private cluster (we want to test end-to-end network realism)?

Victor and I are available Mon 19th 10:00–12:00 PT if you want to run through the amendment and recommended allocation.

Olivia
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@pulsehealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 17 Jul 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging question — credits & seat rebalancing

Hi Olivia — quick note from the CS side. We can host the 60-day Accelerated Inference trial on your private cluster; we’ll provision a pre-warmed pool and capture latency baselines. A few operational points:

- Migration credits: we can apply 120 hours of free migration engineering time (applies to orchestration, KV warm-up, and canary routing).
- Observability: I’ll enable extended retention for the trial traces for 30 days (no charge).
- Rollback: we’ll add automatic fallback policies to route to the hosted pool if any private node health dips below our SLO.

If Rishi confirms the commercial terms (0.7x vs 0.8x), I’ll prepare the technical appendix for the contract amendment and a short runbook for the trial.

Thanks — Monica
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging question — credits & seat rebalancing

Looping in on approvals. Small pricing note: I can approve a 0.8x conversion (instead of 0.7x) if PulseHealth moves to the 12-month renewal and signs the amendment within 21 days. We should reflect that as a conditional line in the amendment ("0.8x applied on execution of 12-month renewal by Aug 11, 2026").

Also recommend we include a one-time onboarding credit of $12,000 to cover their migration hours beyond the included 120 free hours — this keeps the commercial math simple and helps close the ask.

If you two agree, I’ll ask legal to draft the amendment with those conditions and route to DocuSign.

J
